newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Brent indicated steady, NYMEX heat off.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Brent indicated steady, NYMEX heat off.

text.p: SIMEX Brent futures prices were indicated steady at midday on Thursday, but supported by worries over heating oil stocks, brokers said.
November Brent was untraded but quoted at $22.90/$23.15, straddling London's settlement level of $23.10.
Brokers said the Brent market was maintaing the arbitrage against the NYMEX November crude futures contract.
NYMEX November, which fell nine cents in New York to $24.05, was bid at $24.03 on the after-hours ACCESS system at midday in Asia.
November heating oil in New York jumped to a post Gulf War high of 73.15 cents per gallon before ending at 71.98, up 1.22.
On ACCESS, heating oil was last traded at 71.93.
The Energy Information Administration said overnight U.S. heating oil stocks dropped 400,000 barrels in the week to September 27, leaving overall stocks 29 percent lower on the year.
American Petroleum Institute (API) data on Tuesday showed a 17,000 barrel drop in distillate stocks in the U.S., when a build of 1.8 million had been expected.
